get_sequence.description: Returns a single sequence by its unique identifier.
get_sequence.name: get_sequence

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the sequence
parameters.name: sequence_id

parameters.description: Comma-separated relations to expand inline (`owner`, `sequenceSteps`). Max 6.
parameters.name: include

data.description: The response returned by the service.

analytics.description:
Lifetime engagement counts summed over this sequence's steps, grouped by
channel. `linkedIn.repliesReceived` is only on sequences, because Nooks
counts LinkedIn replies per sequence, not per step.

All three groups are always present, with zeros when nothing happened.
Counts are lifetime totals with no date window. They are raw counts, not
rates, so pick your own denominators.

calls.description:
Lifetime call outcome counts. Within a single step, each enrolled
prospect is counted once, by the furthest outcome reached (not once
per dial). Counts nest numerically (meetings ≤ connected ≤ dialed).

meetings.description: Prospects where a meeting was booked

email.description:
Lifetime email engagement counts. `delivered` counts sent emails,
not counting ones that bounced. A recent bounce can stay in
`delivered` until the step sends its next email.

clicked.description: Emails with a tracked link click (requires click tracking)

delivered.description: Emails sent, not counting ones that bounced

objectionReplies.description:
Number of replies that push back on timing, budget, the tool they use
now, or whether the product fits them. These replies also count in
`replied`.

opened.description: Emails opened (requires open tracking to be enabled for the workspace)

positiveReplies.description:
Number of replies that show interest, such as asking for a meeting,
more information or a follow-up. These replies also count in `replied`.

referralReplies.description:
Number of replies that point you to someone else at the company, such
as a better contact or the decision maker. These replies also count in
`replied`.

replied.description:
Number of replies to these emails. Nooks labels each reply by what it
says. `positiveReplies`, `referralReplies` and `objectionReplies` count
the replies with those labels. A reply can have more than one label or
none, so those three counts don't add up to `replied`. Replies that say
no, out-of-office messages and other automatic replies have no count of
their own.

linkedIn.description:
Lifetime LinkedIn engagement counts for sequence-attributed activity.
Only activity tied to a sequence task is counted. LinkedIn connections
imported from the user's existing network and manually logged activity
are excluded. Acceptances are discovered by periodic polling from the
Nooks Chrome extension, so `connectionRequestsAccepted` can lag reality.

connectionRequestsSent.description: Connection requests sent (pending or accepted; withdrawn/failed requests are not counted)

repliesReceived.description:
Inbound LinkedIn messages. Nooks counts each one toward the sequence
it stamped on the conversation at the prospect's first reply.

enabled.description: Whether the sequence is currently active

privacy.description:
Privacy level of the sequence:
- `private`: Only the owner (and workspace managers/admins) can view or edit it in Nooks.
- `team_visible`: All team members can view and enroll prospects; only the owner can edit.
- `team_editable`: All team members can view, enroll prospects, and edit (the default).

Always present. Integrations acting on behalf of a user should
respect this and treat `private` sequences as owner-only.

_href.description: API path to the referenced resource

id.description: Unique identifier of the referenced resource

tags.description:
Tags attached to this sequence, ordered by name; an empty array
when it carries none. Always present. Tags are not a relation, so
they do not sit behind `include=`, and `PATCH /v1/sequences/{id}`
replaces this list wholesale, which is only safe if a caller can
always see what it is about to replace.

Inlined in full rather than as `{ id, _href }` references. Tags
exist for cohort work, so a caller grouping or filtering by tag
needs the names without a further request per sequence. The
embedded `id` is dereferenceable via `GET /v1/tags/{id}`.

items.description:
A workspace tag. Tags group sequences into cohorts so they can be
analysed together (e.g. every "cold" campaign).

A tag's `name` is unique within a workspace, case-insensitively, so a
name identifies a tag just as reliably as its `id` does. `Tags` rows
themselves are untyped. The attachment carries the record type, so
the same tag can in principle span record types.

id.description: Unique identifier for the tag

name.description:
Tag name. Unique per workspace, case-insensitively, so `Cold` and
`cold` are the same tag.

- `date`: Steps are scheduled for specific dates
- `interval`: Steps are scheduled based on intervals from enrollment

updatedAt.description:
Effective last-updated time of the sequence: the most recent of the
sequence's own update time and the update time of any of its steps.
`filter[updatedAt]` applies to this same derived value.

items.description: A sales sequence defining a series of outreach steps

analytics.description:
Lifetime engagement counts summed over this sequence's steps, grouped by
channel. `linkedIn.repliesReceived` is only on sequences, because Nooks
counts LinkedIn replies per sequence, not per step.

All three groups are always present, with zeros when nothing happened.
Counts are lifetime totals with no date window. They are raw counts, not
rates, so pick your own denominators.

calls.description:
Lifetime call outcome counts. Within a single step, each enrolled
prospect is counted once, by the furthest outcome reached (not once
per dial). Counts nest numerically (meetings ≤ connected ≤ dialed).

meetings.description: Prospects where a meeting was booked

email.description:
Lifetime email engagement counts. `delivered` counts sent emails,
not counting ones that bounced. A recent bounce can stay in
`delivered` until the step sends its next email.

clicked.description: Emails with a tracked link click (requires click tracking)

delivered.description: Emails sent, not counting ones that bounced

objectionReplies.description:
Number of replies that push back on timing, budget, the tool they use
now, or whether the product fits them. These replies also count in
`replied`.

opened.description: Emails opened (requires open tracking to be enabled for the workspace)

positiveReplies.description:
Number of replies that show interest, such as asking for a meeting,
more information or a follow-up. These replies also count in `replied`.

referralReplies.description:
Number of replies that point you to someone else at the company, such
as a better contact or the decision maker. These replies also count in
`replied`.

replied.description:
Number of replies to these emails. Nooks labels each reply by what it
says. `positiveReplies`, `referralReplies` and `objectionReplies` count
the replies with those labels. A reply can have more than one label or
none, so those three counts don't add up to `replied`. Replies that say
no, out-of-office messages and other automatic replies have no count of
their own.

linkedIn.description:
Lifetime LinkedIn engagement counts for sequence-attributed activity.
Only activity tied to a sequence task is counted. LinkedIn connections
imported from the user's existing network and manually logged activity
are excluded. Acceptances are discovered by periodic polling from the
Nooks Chrome extension, so `connectionRequestsAccepted` can lag reality.

connectionRequestsSent.description: Connection requests sent (pending or accepted; withdrawn/failed requests are not counted)

repliesReceived.description:
Inbound LinkedIn messages. Nooks counts each one toward the sequence
it stamped on the conversation at the prospect's first reply.

description: Read prospects, accounts, sequences, calls and emails, manage standalone tasks, and watch records for changes.

nooks_new_account_trigger.description: Runs for each new account in Nooks. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

nooks_new_call_trigger.description: Runs for each new call in Nooks. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.
